title: close_task comment write-channel: apply the loop-mode author:'uat' guard to close_task's comment param (TASK-108 defense-in-depth)
description:
Follow-up minted from the TASK-108 gating review (rev-108, APPROVE, 2026-07-14). TASK-108 narrowed the loop-mode uat-comment fabrication channel at the append_comment write seam (loopModeUatCommentGuard refuses author:'uat' in loop mode without a uat_delegated_to_orchestrator grant). The reviewer confirmed a SECOND, still-open write path: close_task's own `comment` param reaches appendComment via closeTask WITHOUT passing through loopModeUatCommentGuard.

This is NOT exploitable for a one-shot self-authorized uat-only close: closeTask runs loopModeCloseGuard (Gate 2 read-time check on PRE-EXISTING on-disk comments) and only appends the new comment AFTER the guard passes, atomically — so a loop caller cannot plant its own marker and pass Gate 2 in the same call (the existing TASK-082 regression lock proves this). The residual leak is cosmetic/defense-in-depth: a close_task call can still land an author:'uat' comment on disk (e.g. on a non-uat-only ticket, where Gate 2 consults no uat comments) with no delegation check. Wiring the same guard into close_task's comment path closes the write-channel asymmetry so both append seams enforce the identical loop-mode author:'uat' rule.

ROOT CAUSE / FIX DIRECTION: src/mcp-server.js close_task handler (and/or src/task-store.js closeTask) appends comment.author without the loopModeUatCommentGuard check that append_comment now has. Apply loopModeUatCommentGuard({ repoRoot, author: comment.author }) before the close's comment write, keeping task-store decoupled (inject via the MCP layer, same pattern as loopModeCloseGuard/loopModeUatCommentGuard). Must NOT break the legitimate close flow: the orchestrator's own author:'orchestrator' closing comment is unaffected (only author:'uat' is gated), and a delegated loop close (uat_delegated_to_orchestrator=true) must still record. Keep all TASK-099 + TASK-108 matrix specs green. Rebuild+commit dist/ (mcp-server bundles); dist-parity green.
acceptance_criteria: In loop mode without a uat_delegated_to_orchestrator grant, a close_task call whose comment.author==='uat' is refused at the same guard seam as append_comment (typed error, e.g. reuse UatCommentGuardError / LOOP_UAT_COMMENT_DENIED) BEFORE the comment is written to disk — red-first spec against today's ungated close_task comment path.

The legitimate close flow is unaffected: author:'orchestrator' (and any non-'uat' author) closing comments still land in loop mode; a delegated loop close (uat_delegated_to_orchestrator===true) still records an author:'uat' comment; harness mode is unaffected — each proven by spec.
All existing TASK-099 and TASK-108 matrix specs remain unmodified and green (close-guard / mcp-close-task / mcp-append-comment-uat-guard / task-board).
dist/ rebuilt and committed if src/mcp-server.js or src/task-store.js changed; dist-parity green.

SKILL.md Gate 2 documentation (both parity copies) updated to note that BOTH write seams (append_comment and close_task's comment) now enforce the loop-mode author:'uat' rule, so no residual write-channel asymmetry remains.
